# India and 1991

<!-- STEP id="start" -->
For many years after Independence, India followed a state-led approach, similar to a planned economy. Firms needed licences and permits from the government. Banking, transport and heavy industries were mostly in the public sector.

<!-- STEP id="crisis" -->
By 1991, the country faced serious economic difficulties. As a result, the government made major economic reforms.

<!-- STEP id="reform" -->
The reforms cut excessive rules, encouraged private enterprise, opened the economy to trade and investment with other countries, and increased competition. India moved towards a more market-oriented system. The government still kept an important role.

**India changed the balance between government and market. The government kept an important role.**
